title: Everywhere-defined derived functors
statement: Pointwise essentially constant ind and pro diagrams assemble into derived functors RF and LG with universal comparison transformations.

proof.text: Quasi-isomorphisms in each homotopy category admit both calculi of fractions, as supplied by Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Fractions. Write QA and QB for the localization functors, and Fh and Gh for the homotopy functors followed by QB and QA respectively.

For each K, unpack the essentially constant ind-diagram as a cocone p with stage j0 and section s. This cocone is a colimit: its map to another cocone v is s followed by v at j0; the common-stage factorization proves the leg equations, and the section equation proves uniqueness. Extend p to the costructured-arrow diagram of QA at QA(K): represent its structural arrow by a left fraction (f,t), and use Fh(f) followed by p at t. The common-refinement equality criterion and naturality of p prove independence of the representative; applying this to a composed numerator proves naturality. The identity numerator recovers every inverse-denominator leg. Restrict any other cocone along t mapped to QA(t) inverse and use the denominator colimit. Each costructured arrow maps to its representing inverse denominator by its numerator, so naturality proves the extended cocone is a colimit. This is QA.HasPointwiseLeftKanExtensionAt Fh (QA.obj K). All these constructions are proved in the private helpers of the item module.

For each M, unpack the pro-diagram witness into its cone u and its retraction/factorization data. Apply leftDerived_defined_pointwiseKan_bridge with WB, QB, Gh, M and the supplied value. Its first conclusion gives QB.HasPointwiseRightKanExtensionAt Gh (QB.obj M).

Use Functor.hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctorAt_iff and its left-derived counterpart to install HasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor Fh WA and HasPointwiseLeftDerivedFunctor Gh WB. Mathlib pointwise derived existence instances now supply HasRightDerivedFunctor and HasLeftDerivedFunctor. Take RF = Fh.totalRightDerived QA WA, LG = Gh.totalLeftDerived QB WB, beta = totalRightDerivedUnit and alpha = totalLeftDerivedCounit. Their IsRightDerivedFunctor and IsLeftDerivedFunctor instances give the two conjuncts, with no adjunction hypothesis or new unproved theorem.

proof_origin.place: Definition 05S9 and Lemma 05SA, implemented via pointwise Kan extensions; the ind-diagram construction uses Categories 04VE and 04VF, and the pro-diagram construction reuses the proved left-derived pointwise Kan bridge.

lean.statement: theorem exists_everywhere_defined_derived_functors {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB} [Category.{vA} A] [Category.{vB} B] [Abelian A] [Abelian B] [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{wB} B] (F : A ⥤ B) (G : B ⥤ A) [F.Additive] [G.Additive] (hR : ∀ K : HomotopyCategory A (ComplexShape.up ℤ), let W := HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) let D := MorphismProperty.Under.forget W ⊤ K ⋙ Under.forget K ⋙ F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ∃ X : DerivedCategory B, IsEssentiallyConstantIndDiagram D X) (hL : ∀ M : HomotopyCategory B (ComplexShape.up ℤ), let W := HomotopyCategory.quasiIso B (ComplexShape.up ℤ) let D := MorphismProperty.Over.forget W ⊤ M ⋙ Over.forget M ⋙ G.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ∃ X : DerivedCategory A, IsEssentiallyConstantProDiagram D X) : ∃ (RF : DerivedCategory A ⥤ DerivedCategory B) (LG : DerivedCategory B ⥤ DerivedCategory A) (β : F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF) (α : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ LG ⟶ G.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh), RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor β (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧ LG.IsLeftDerivedFunctor α (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso B (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
